raw_response:
I will do it close to how I did last year, only a little tighter on money and a little heavier on the crops that feed the house steady. I have 8.5 mu, not a big place, so I cannot gamble. I will keep wheat on 3.5 mu because wheat is steady here and with well water I can hold it up if spring is dry. I will put 2.5 mu in maize and 2.5 mu in sunflower. For seed, I will use the kinds I saw do well in nearby fields, not the old weak seed. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the field stay thin. For wheat I will feed it the heaviest, because if wheat stools well and fills grain, that is money in hand. For maize I will still give enough base fertilizer and one topdressing, because if maize goes pale after knee-high, yield drops fast. Sunflower I will not overfeed with nitrogen, or it grows too much stalk and lodging can come, but I will still give some bottom fertilizer so the head fills better. Since I have well irrigation, I will give wheat three waters if the season asks, maize two, sunflower one. I do most things the way people around me do when they get a clean stand and decent harvest. I will plough or rotary till where it helps the land stay loose, and I will spray when I see real pest pressure, not just for show.
